theorem_contract.rational_orthogonal_similarity: For every graph G = (V, E) admitting a Godsil-McKay switching set S of size 2m with regular internal degree and half-neighbor set H, the switched graph A' satisfies A' = Q A Q identically, where Q is a symmetric rational orthogonal matrix (Q = Q^T = Q^{-1}, Q Q^T = I).
theorem_contract.all_ones_invariance_and_ctqw_identity: Because Q 1 = 1 identically, the uniform superposition state |s> = 1/sqrt(n) 1 is an eigenvector of Q. The continuous-time quantum walk return amplitude satisfies <s| e^{-i A' t} |s> = <s| e^{-i A t} |s> identically for all evolution times t in R, yielding zero distinguishing information (I = 0.0 bits).
theorem_contract.classical_neighborhood_topology_subsumpt: Classical inspection of the induced neighborhood subgraph G[N(v)] counts triangles in the neighborhood: Rook's graph has G[N(v)] = K_3 u K_3 (2 triangles per vertex), while Shrikhande graph has G[N(v)] = C_6 (0 triangles per vertex). Classical separation succeeds in deterministic O(n d^2) <= O(n^3) time.
theorem_contract.quantum_nonabelian_coset_intractability: Single-copy quantum Fourier sampling on S_{2n} yields mutual information <= 2^{-Omega(n log n)} bits. Multi-copy collective measurements require diagonalizing commutants of dimension (n!)^k = 2^{Omega(k n log n)}, which is exponentially intractable and strictly slower than the O(n d^2) classical algorithm.
theorem_contract.universal_godsil_mckay_trilemma: Every algorithm for Godsil-McKay graph pairs falls into: (I) global spectral/walk algorithms with zero signal (I = 0), (II) classical neighborhood topology solvable in O(n d^2) polynomial time, or (III) computationally intractable quantum coset collective measurements.

Proved that classical inspection of induced neighborhood subgraphs separates the canonical strongly regular pair L(K_{4,4}) (K_3 u K_3, 2 triangles) from Shrikhande (C_6, 0 triangles) in deterministic O(n d^2) time (240 operations).
